Solution 1 has a sign error: since $\Delta \log|x| = 2\pi\delta$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $\Delta_x \int_\Omega \log|x-y|\,u(y)\,dy = +2\pi u(x)$, not $-2\pi u(x)$. Solution 2 wrongly claims that $A \neq 0$ forces $\phi$ to be constant, but $\phi = (B - Ru)/A$ is not constant because $Ru$ is not constant in general. Solution 3 reaches $C = 2\pi/|\Omega|$ correctly but then arbitrarily sets $|\Omega| = \pi$, which the problem does not justify.

The correct derivation gives $u \equiv K$ and $C = 2\pi/|\Omega|$. This is consistent: with $u \equiv K$, $\phi(x) = \frac{1}{|\Omega|}\int_\Omega \log|x-y|\,dy + \text{const}$, and $\Delta\phi = 2\pi/|\Omega|$ on $\Omega$. None of the three final answers ($-2\pi/|\Omega|$, $0$, $2$) matches this.
